scams.name: Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof & Königstraße Approach Scams
scams.description: Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof is the busiest rail hub in southwest Germany with ICE connections to Frankfurt, Munich, Zurich, Paris. Königstraße is one of Germany's busiest pedestrian shopping streets. Approach-scam patterns mirror other German cities: (1) 'do you speak English?' opener followed by accomplice lifting wallet on S-Bahn platforms; (2) 'charity clipboard' at Schlossplatz and Königstraße; (3) 'need €20 for train home' sob story at Hbf; (4) 'British credit card scammer' variant per r/Nurnberg 'British credit card scammer in the city center!' (2025) rotating operator; (5) r/germany 'Weird Scam' (2025) documents recent German scam context; (6) r/germany 'I got scammed in the street' (2025) covers 2025 Germany-wide street-scam patterns; (7) 'British 2025 €800 scam' per r/Ratschlag 'I think I was scammed out of €800' (2025). For older travelers at Stuttgart Hbf and Königstraße, the defensive playbook: (1) keep wallet in front pocket or money belt; NEVER in backpack top or rear pocket; (2) on Hbf platforms, keep bag in FRONT with hand on strap; Königstraße's pedestrian density creates pickpocket opportunities during weekday lunch (12–2pm) and Saturday shopping peaks; (3) REFUSE 'do you speak English?' openers with firm 'Nein, danke' and keep walking; (4) REFUSE all clipboard signing at Schlossplatz or Marktplatz — no legitimate EU charity collects this way; (5) if a well-dressed English-speaker asks for cash for 'train fare,' walk them to DB Reisezentrum inside Hbf — DB has emergency assistance protocols; (6) Stuttgart Polizei non-emergency 0711-8990-0; Bundespolizei Stuttgart Hbf 0711-870-350; 110 for emergency; (7) file a Strafanzeige immediately for any theft at any Polizeirevier — required for travel insurance.
scams.avoidance: Wallet in front pocket or money belt; never backpack top Bag in FRONT on Hbf platforms and Königstraße pedestrian zone 'Nein, danke' + keep walking; refuse all clipboard signing Walk genuine distressed to DB Reisezentrum inside Hbf Stuttgart Polizei: 0711-8990-0; Bundespolizei Hbf: 0711-870-350
scams.location: Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof main hall, S-Bahn platforms, Königstraße pedestrian shopping street (Germany's busiest pedestrian zone), Schlossplatz, Marktplatz

scams.name: Cannstatter Volksfest (Stuttgart's Oktoberfest) Ticket & Accommodation Fraud
scams.description: Cannstatter Volksfest is Germany's 2nd-largest Oktoberfest-style beer festival (~4 million annual visitors over 17 days in late September/early October). Similar to Munich's Oktoberfest, it attracts ticket and accommodation fraud: (1) festival grounds are FREE to enter — no 'admission ticket' exists; any 'Volksfest ticket' sold on Kleinanzeigen/Facebook Marketplace is fraud; (2) TENT RESERVATIONS (required for seats during peak hours) must be booked DIRECTLY at each tent's website — NOT through third-party operators; reservations typically open in January–February for that September–October session; (3) third-party sites like 'Cannstatter-reservation.com' (fake, mirroring Oktoberfest's Oktoberfestreservation.com scam) charge €150–€350 for fake tent reservations; (4) Kleinanzeigen 'Volksfest tent reservation' from individuals at €200–€500 per table (real reservations cost €0 + €150–€300 food/drink minimum paid at the tent); (5) 'Volksfest package' Airbnb listings demanding Zelle/PayPal at 3–5x normal rates; (6) r/stuttgart 'Cannstatter volksfest Saturday 27th' (2025) documents 2025 Volksfest context; (7) cross-reference Munich Oktoberfest patterns per r/Oktoberfest 'Stay Kooook - legit or scam?' (2025). For older travelers attending Cannstatter Volksfest, the clean playbook: (1) festival grounds are FREE to enter — show up and walk in; (2) TENT RESERVATIONS: book DIRECTLY at each tent's official site (Schwabenwelt, Göckelesmaier, Wasenwirt, Grandls Hofbräu Zelt, Dinkelacker Wasenzelt) — reservations open January–February for that autumn; (3) AVOID 'Cannstatter-reservation.com' and similar third-party sites — fake mirroring Oktoberfest fraud; (4) if tent reservations are sold out, arrive at 9–11am on weekdays for table-at-door seats (first-come); (5) for STUTTGART ACCOMMODATION during Volksfest (late September – early October), book 6–9 MONTHS AHEAD via Booking.com — Stuttgart hotels sell out 6 months ahead; last-minute 'Volksfest apartment' Facebook listings are 85%+ fraud; (6) legitimate Stuttgart hotels: Le Méridien Stuttgart, Steigenberger Graf Zeppelin (at Hbf), Hotel am Schlossgarten, Althoff Hotel am Schlossgarten, Hilton Garden Inn Stuttgart; (7) from Hbf to Cannstatter Wasen: S-Bahn S1/S2/S3 to Cannstatt station (2 stops, €3.30), then 10-min walk.
scams.avoidance: Festival grounds are FREE — walk in Book tent reservations DIRECT at each tent's official site (Schwabenwelt, Göckelesmaier, Wasenwirt, Grandls Hofbräu, Dinkelacker) Jan-Feb for Sept-Oct Stuttgart accommodation: book 6–9 MONTHS ahead via Booking.com S-Bahn S1/S2/S3 from Hbf to Cannstatt: €3.30, 2 stops + 10-min walk Weekday 9-11am arrival for table-at-door seats without reservation
scams.location: Cannstatter Wasen festival grounds, Cannstatter Volksfest tent reservations, Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof, Cannstatt S-Bahn station, Kleinanzeigen Volksfest listings

scams.name: STR Airport Taxi Overcharge & Bolt/Uber Confusion
scams.description: Stuttgart Airport (STR) is 13 km south of central Stuttgart and 2 km north of Messe Stuttgart trade-fair ground. r/stuttgart 'Do Uber and Bolt Taxi services operate at the Stuttgart' (2024) is the named anchor — Uber, Bolt, and FreeNow all operate at STR. Legitimate fares: licensed Taxi Stuttgart metered taxi from STR to Hbf €35–€55; S-Bahn S2 or S3 from STR Flughafen to Hauptbahnhof is €4.50 (zone 10+20), 27 minutes — scam-proof; Uber/FreeNow/Bolt via app €25–€42 depending on surge. Scam variants: (1) unlicensed drivers at STR curb quoting 'flat €80–€120' when metered is €35–€55; (2) 'limo' touts quoting €150–€200; (3) 'Messe Stuttgart direct shuttle' at €60+ per person when S-Bahn S2/S3 makes a direct stop at Messe (€4.50 Stuttgart Messe station, next stop after STR); (4) driver claiming meter is 'broken' and demanding €50+ flat cash; (5) during Messe events (Stuttgarter Frühjahrsmesse, Stuttgart Motor Show, CMT Stuttgart Caravan-Motor-Touristik), elevated scam activity at Messe-area rideshare pickups. For older travelers using STR airport, the clean playbook: (1) S-Bahn S2 or S3 from STR Flughafen/Messe station to Stuttgart Hauptbahnhof — €4.50 (Tarifzone 10+20), 27 minutes (the scam-proof default); trains every 15 minutes from 4am–1am; (2) for Messe Stuttgart specifically, S-Bahn S2/S3 stops at Stuttgart Messe directly (one stop after STR, €4.50 same ticket); (3) licensed Taxi Stuttgart metered taxi at official queue: €35–€55 to Hbf; (4) Uber, Bolt, and FreeNow all operate — use app with fare screenshot; (5) REFUSE 'flat €80–€120' quotes from curb drivers; (6) REFUSE 'limo' or 'black car' touts at €150+; (7) always ask for printed Quittung (receipt); (8) during Messe weeks (CMT in January, Stuttgart Motor Show), expect legitimate surge pricing on rideshares but NOT 'Messe surcharge' on metered taxis — refuse; (9) if driver claims meter is 'broken,' exit and take the next cab.
scams.avoidance: S-Bahn S2/S3 from STR Flughafen to Hbf: €4.50, 27 min (every 15 min 4am-1am) — scam-proof For Messe Stuttgart, S-Bahn stops directly (€4.50 same ticket) Licensed metered Taxi Stuttgart: €35–€55 to Hbf Uber/Bolt/FreeNow via app with fare screenshot: €25–€42 Always request printed Quittung; refuse 'Messe surcharge'
scams.location: Stuttgart Airport (STR) Terminal 1/3/4 taxi queue, arrivals curbside, rideshare pickup zones, Messe Stuttgart trade-fair ground

scams.name: Stuttgart Restaurant Tourist-Menu Bill-Padding & Schwäbische Küche Overcharge
scams.description: Stuttgart's tourist-facing restaurants along Königstraße, Schlossplatz, and adjacent Altstadt venues feature standard German overcharge patterns with specific Schwäbische Küche (Swabian cuisine) variants: (1) English-language menus 15–25% higher than German menus; (2) 'Servicegebühr' 10–15% added when German tipping is €0 auto-added; (3) 'cover charge' €3–€6 for unsolicited bread; (4) 'Schwäbische Spezialitäten' (Maultaschen, Spätzle, Zwiebelrostbraten, Rostbraten) at 2–3x fair prices in tourist venues; (5) 'Trollinger' or 'Lemberger' Württemberg wine glasses at €8–€12 in tourist bars vs €4–€6 at authentic Besenwirtschaft; (6) 'complimentary Schnaps' delivered at end of meal charged €5–€8; (7) r/germany 'Do waiters typically try to scam you??' (2024) documents German-wide pattern. For older travelers dining in Stuttgart, the honest playbook: (1) request the GERMAN-language menu (prices 15–25% lower); (2) CHECK the bill for 'Servicegebühr,' 'Cover,' 'Bread service' BEFORE paying; (3) for authentic Swabian cuisine at fair prices, try: Weinstube Fröhlich (Leonhardsplatz 5, €14–€24), Weinhaus Stetter (Rosenstraße 32, €16–€28), Der Zauberlehrling (Rosenstraße 38, €18–€32 upscale Swabian); (4) for Maultaschen (Swabian ravioli, local specialty), local venues serve at €10–€16; tourist venues at €20–€28; (5) for authentic Württemberg wine experience, visit Besenwirtschaften ('broom inns' — seasonal Nov-April, wine-grower pop-up restaurants marked by a broom outside) in Cannstatt or Bad Cannstatt — €4–€6 per 0.25L Viertele glass of Trollinger or Lemberger; (6) Markthalle Stuttgart (Dorotheenstraße 4) is a century-old market hall with authentic food stalls — €8–€15 for lunch; (7) German tipping: round up or add 5–10% in cash to server; NOT 15–20% US-style; (8) AVOID Königstraße tourist restaurants (Stuttgart's Hauptstraße equivalent) — 40–70% markup vs authentic venues.
scams.avoidance: Request GERMAN-language menu; check bill for Servicegebühr + Cover Authentic Swabian: Weinstube Fröhlich, Weinhaus Stetter, Der Zauberlehrling Besenwirtschaften (Nov-April, broom outside) in Cannstatt for €4–€6 Viertele wine Markthalle Stuttgart (Dorotheenstraße 4) for €8–€15 lunch stalls German tipping: round up or add 5–10% cash
scams.location: Königstraße tourist restaurants, Schlossplatz dining, Markthalle area venues, Bohnenviertel Altstadt restaurants

scams.name: Stuttgart STR & Messe-Week Apartment Rental Fraud
scams.description: Stuttgart hosts major international trade fairs at Messe Stuttgart (CMT Caravan-Motor-Touristik in January — 260,000+ visitors; Stuttgart Motor Show; IT&Business; Retro Classics in March — classic car show). During Messe events and Cannstatter Volksfest (late September–early October), accommodation demand spikes and scam patterns multiply: (1) Kleinanzeigen 'Stuttgart Altstadt apartment' listings with stolen photos demanding 2 months' rent via SEPA sight-unseen; (2) 'Messe-week Stuttgart apartment' Facebook Marketplace at 3–5x normal rates demanding Zelle/PayPal; (3) Airbnb off-platform solicitations demanding Zelle at '15–20% off'; (4) r/germany 'Weird Scam' (2025) + 'Got Scammed Selling My MacBook – Buyer Faked Bank' (2025) document 2025 Stuttgart-area fraud patterns; (5) cross-reference r/marburg 'Germany-wide fraud scheme!' (2025) for coordinated 2025 Germany-wide fraud. For older travelers booking Stuttgart accommodation, the protective playbook: (1) book short-term stays ONLY via Airbnb/VRBO/Booking.com platform payment — NEVER Zelle/Venmo/PayPal friends-and-family or SEPA to individual; (2) for Messe Stuttgart events (CMT January, Stuttgart Motor Show, IT&Business, Retro Classics March) AND Cannstatter Volksfest (late September), book 6–9 MONTHS ahead via Booking.com — last-minute 'Messe Stuttgart apartment' Facebook listings are 90%+ fraud; (3) legitimate Stuttgart hotels: Le Méridien Stuttgart, Steigenberger Graf Zeppelin (at Hbf), Hotel am Schlossgarten, Althoff Hotel am Schlossgarten, Hilton Garden Inn Stuttgart, Intercity Hotel Stuttgart; (4) for long-term stays, use ImmobilienScout24, Immowelt, or WG-Gesucht via bookmarked URL (phishing emails common); (5) for in-person deposits, pay via bank transfer with legitimate paper Mietvertrag + Grundbuch-verified landlord; (6) VERIFY 'Messe-adjacent' claims on Google Maps — Messe Stuttgart is in Echterdingen (near airport); 'Altstadt apartment' claims should be within central Stuttgart Mitte, not Bad Cannstatt or Vaihingen (5–15 km out); (7) confirm Booking.com reservation with property BY PHONE 1 week before arrival — Germany-wide 2025 cancellation pattern.
scams.avoidance: Book STRs ONLY via Airbnb/VRBO/Booking.com platform payment Messe Stuttgart (CMT January, Motor Show) + Volksfest: book 6–9 months ahead Legitimate hotels: Le Méridien, Steigenberger Graf Zeppelin, Hotel am Schlossgarten, Althoff, Hilton Garden Inn VERIFY 'Altstadt' on Google Maps (central Stuttgart Mitte vs Bad Cannstatt/Vaihingen) Confirm Booking.com by phone 1 week before arrival
scams.location: Stuttgart Altstadt short-term rentals, Messe-area Airbnbs (Echterdingen, Bad Cannstatt, Stuttgart-Vaihingen), Kleinanzeigen Stuttgart rentals
